"StreamHub ngeri nnyangu era nteefu ey'okulabiramu firimu n'ebitundutundu ku Android. Buli kimu kiri mu kifo kimu, n'olwekyo osobola okunoonyereza ku bimanyiddwa ennyo, okunoonya ekintu ekimu, oba okweyongera mu kifo we wakoma.
Ebiwandiiko eby'obuvvuunuzi binoonyezebwa ne bitegekebwa mu budde ku lulwo mu nnimi nnyingi, buli mutwe gulina ensibuko eziwera, era ky'olabako kiyinza okusindikibwa ku Chromecast oba ku ttivi ey'omulembe. App ekola ku ssimu, ku tabuleti, ku Android TV ne ku Fire TV, era akawunti ey'okwesalirawo eterekera olukalala lwo n'ebyafaayo byo nga bifaanana ku byonna.
StreamHub ekolebwa ttiimu ntono egikozesa buli lunaku, era yeeyongera obulungi olw'ebyo abantu bye batubuulira."

StreamHub is an independent media front-end for Android. It does not host, store, upload, transmit or control any video, audio, subtitle or other media content. Everything played through the app is provided by third-party sources that are not affiliated with, endorsed by or controlled by StreamHub, and that may change or disappear at any time. StreamHub claims no ownership of third-party content and does not authorise copyright infringement. You are solely responsible for ensuring that your use of the app and of any source complies with the copyright, licensing and other laws that apply where you are. Requests to remove or disable access to content should be directed to the third-party source or rights holder concerned, as StreamHub holds no content to remove. Title and artwork metadata is provided by The Movie Database (TMDB). StreamHub is not endorsed or certified by TMDB. Subtitles may come from OpenSubtitles and may be machine-translated, so their accuracy and timing are not guaranteed. Netflix, IMDb, TMDB, OpenSubtitles, Google, Chromecast, Android TV, Google TV, Fire TV, Amazon, ExoPlayer, Media3, DLNA and all other names and trademarks are used for identification only and imply no sponsorship, endorsement or affiliation.
